gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.hint: on the point of happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' expresses something on the point of happening: is about to start.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: While the chef ___ the sauce, the waiter set the tables.
gaps.hint: while frames the longer simultaneous action
gaps.explanation: 'While' frames the longer simultaneous action, which takes the past continuous: was preparing.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ for over two hours.
gaps.hint: for over two hours up to now
gaps.explanation: A duration continuing up to the present moment takes the present perfect continuous: have been chatting.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me yesterday to say she had arrived safely.
gaps.hint: yesterday fixes a finished past action
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the past simple is used: phoned.
